Saturated fatty acids contain cis double bonds that kink their chains, letting them pack tightly.

Unsaturated fatty acids contain more hydrogen atoms, forming stronger hydrogen bonds between chains.
Saturated fatty acids are polar and therefore dissolve readily in water at room temperature.
Unsaturated fatty acids are always much shorter, which is what lowers their melting point.
